source_revision.algorithm: SHA-256 of '<file-sha256><two spaces><repository-relative-path><LF>' in bytewise path order
source_revision.scope: kernel/Cargo.toml, kernel/Cargo.lock, kernel/src/**/*.rs and wit/wasm-biotic/*.wit; this self-referential inventory is excluded

conformance.reason: For the exact graph and bounded-external profile named by a conforming release bundle, every factory role, service, workflow and policy executes as a Wasm component. The reachable native kernel is limited to the eight declared generic substrate mechanisms and does not implement factory semantics. Admission requires a canonical Ed25519 certificate over the exact component/package closure and this inventory, verified against an independently persisted operator public key; native code treats semantic reports as opaque, digest-bound evidence. A release claim is valid only when this exact inventory, its signed package cohort, the optimized native artifact and the public-key-verifiable conformance reports are retained together by a content-addressed release manifest. HTTP is a generic byte-transport mechanism whose effective authority is the intersection of an exact signed per-principal constraint and immutable operator capacity; it does not move workflow or provider semantics into native code.
enforced_invariants: receipt executor identity remains the authoritative raw graph-node digest
derived executable identity and source provenance are persisted separately
R2 static composition retains one independently recomputed principal per source node and rewrites every direct host import to its content-derived per-consumer alias
R2 root and dynamic executables expose only the exact alias set in their signed static closure; retained v1 packages remain on the explicit graph-union compatibility path
component-runner operations, clock wakes, activation handles and transaction idempotency are graph-qualified and principal-bound

R2 activation commit atomically transfers exactly one handle owner from the source graph principal to the admitted target graph's exact same principal seed only when that target principal retains the activation/switch import; rollback applies the same rule to the verified last-known-good graph
native operator evidence inspection can read a persisted generic completion but is not linked into any component world and cannot satisfy guest poll or cancel authority
every R2 alias call records its enclosing executable, graph-qualified runtime principal, exact request digest and stable success or failure outcome

R2 legacy RunRequest grants are canonical non-escalating compatibility and resource metadata derived from the target executable's signed principal closure; callable authority remains exclusively the immutable selected alias context
local configuration cannot exceed manifest-bound ceilings or namespaces
every admission must carry a valid canonical certificate binding the exact release closure and this compiled native inventory
offline semantic validation report bytes are hashed but never interpreted by native code
first active-root bootstrap and selection require the immutable operator-pinned manifest digest; inactive candidate admission remains possible
root exports cannot run unless their manifest is the durable active manifest

bounded HTTP operations are owned by the exact graph, principal seed, alias and constraint digest; the dispatch boundary and terminal receipt are durable and a possibly dispatched operation is never automatically retried
HTTP destinations, methods, headers, DNS answers, TLS peers, credentials and resource budgets are the runtime intersection of signed v3 authority and immutable operator v2 capacity

operator_capacity.successor_rule: graph requirements must fit capacity; effective root fuel and memory are the graph/operator minimum

release_certification.private_key_location: external offline certifier only; never release or mechanism state

activation.mechanism: operator-pinned exact first-manifest trust plus independently pinned release-certifier public key, atomic exact verified-manifest selection, active BlobRef resolution and last-known-good restoration; an R2 commit or rollback atomically rekeys its one principal-owned handle to the verified destination graph's exact same principal seed and activation/switch import

clock.mechanism: wall clock plus explicitly requested durable principal-owned wakes; past or equal deadlines are immediately due and only future delay is horizon-bounded

component-runner.mechanism: manifest-edge-authorized exact-digest Component Model instantiation with principal-owned operation lifecycle plus fuel, memory, output and wall-time bounds; R2 legacy request grants are bounded by the canonical executable principal closure and cannot install callable authority

http-transport.mechanism: exact alias-bound signed v3 constraints intersected with immutable operator v2 capacity; HTTPS-only explicit HTTP/1.1 framing, one-shot DNS with full-answer CIDR rejection and pinned selected address, TLS1.3 WebPKI validation plus signed SPKI pins, no redirects or retries, bounded URL/method/header/body/time/concurrency, opaque owner-only credential injection with reflection rejection, and durable owner-qualified dispatch/outcome records

key-service.mechanism: non-exported Ed25519 key material plus OS secure entropy

transaction-store.mechanism: opaque exact-scope key-to-blob CAS transactions with principal-qualified idempotency

network: Rust standard-library TCP sockets and one-shot DNS only in src/http_transport.rs
rustls 0.23.38 TLS1.3 with WebPKI roots, optional owner-only operator DER roots and signed peer-SPKI pins
explicit bounded HTTP/1.1 adapter with no proxy, redirect, cookie, compression or retry machinery
keys: ring 0.17.14 Ed25519 and system secure random

operating_system_dependencies: configured-root filesystem persistence and fsync/rename semantics
Rust standard-library memory, synchronization and timer threads
operating-system DNS resolver and TCP socket stack for explicitly enabled bounded HTTP
standard input/output for the generic local launcher transport

http_operator_capacity_example.authority: operator-reviewed explicit external transport capacity; never package-selected

verification_harness.durability_fault_controller: policy-neutral one-shot controller available only through the explicit conformance constructor; ordinary constructors and the production CLI install a disarmed controller and expose no input that can arm it
verification_harness.durability_fault_matrix: covers blob and component content writes, transaction and audit commits, component and HTTP dispatch/completion/receipt replay, HTTP pre-dispatch cancellation and post-boundary indeterminate no-retry recovery, activation commit/rollback/boot recovery with paired opaque graph/state pointers, stale two-handle writer fencing, and principal-owned runner, wake and activation handles across restart, including one-owner activation handoff to an admitted target with the exact seed/import and rejection of stale-source, wrong-seed and missing-import access
verification_harness.operator_evidence_inspection: read-only native inspection returns a persisted generic component completion; the same R2 operation remains inaccessible to unscoped or wrong-principal component-runner WIT poll and cancel calls

limitations: The accepted executable cache is bound through canonical manifest metadata and a derivation descriptor; independent recomposition is release evidence rather than native policy.
Semantic role coverage and complete-graph execution are release evidence produced outside the native kernel; the kernel neither interprets nor substitutes for those proofs.

Bounded HTTP is available only when both immutable operator v2 capacity and an exact signed v3 per-principal constraint enable it; v1/v2 signed profiles and v1 operator capacity remain transport-disabled.

The native HTTP adapter implements only generic byte transport and enforcement. Origin identities, credential handles and request data are opaque; provider protocol, workflow, retry policy and response meaning remain component semantics.

R2 per-consumer authority depends on signed deterministic import rewriting and composition; the kernel independently re-derives every principal and alias, verifies the raw/scoped/executable surfaces and links no canonical host imports on the R2 path.

The in-process authority trace is diagnostic runtime evidence; durable authority is carried by the signed principal inventory, admitted graph bindings, principal-qualified operation records and execution provenance.
Key handles are operator-issued bearer capabilities behind an explicit per-consumer key-service grant; components cannot create, enumerate or export native key material.

The component-owned capability services are bounded deterministic reference services; this release does not claim feature parity with unrestricted compilers, workspaces, providers or deployment systems.
The v1 certifier public key is immutable after mechanism initialization; explicit operator key rotation and revocation governance remain outside package authority.
The retained optimized native artifact is exact to its attested host target and toolchain. Another operating system, architecture or toolchain requires a new native attestation and release bundle.
